name: Socialism
summary: Socialism holds that the main means of production should be under social, democratic control rather than private ownership, whether through public, cooperative or collective forms. Its critique of capitalism centres on exploitation, domination at work, inequality, alienation and crisis, and its aim is production for need and, in the Marxist tradition, eventual distribution by need. The family divides over markets versus planning, reform versus revolution, and how far the state should be used or dismantled.
scope: The broad mainstream socialist family as described in the Wikipedia and Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy accounts, anchored in Marx and Engels's Communist Manifesto and Marx's Critique of the Gotha Programme. Where strands differ (democratic vs authoritarian, market vs planned, reformist vs revolutionary) answers follow the documented majority view or score 0 when split. It excludes the narrower Leninist, anarchist, social-democratic and national-socialist strands, which have their own profiles.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Universal public services such as health care are standard in social-democratic and democratic-socialist programmes, and socialists treat basic needs as a collective responsibility.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Socialist and labour-movement programmes back wage floors and collective bargaining as ways of improving workers' share, though many treat them as palliatives short of ending wage dependence.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Socialists hold that unregulated markets produce crises, externalities and concentrated power, and even market socialists want ownership and investment under social control.

public-ownership.rationale: Social ownership of the bulk of the means of production, in public, cooperative or collective form, is the defining proposal, and energy, rail and utilities are the standard cases.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The Manifesto's second measure is a heavy progressive income tax, and redistribution from owners of capital is a constant in socialist programmes.

unions-good.rationale: Syndicalists, libertarian socialists and social democrats all champion trade unions and collective bargaining as the workers' organised power.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Manifesto sums up communist theory as abolition of bourgeois private property, and socialists subordinate property rights to social ownership.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Social democrats back regulation and socialists note capitalism's externalities, but socialists generally want to change ownership rather than only regulate it, so agreement is moderate.

cut-welfare.rationale: Universal welfare services are core to social democracy and defended across the socialist family; cutting them as dependency-creating is the opposing view.

worker-ownership.rationale: Employee and cooperative ownership is one recognised form of social ownership, and workers' councils and cooperatives are key vehicles, but state and community forms are equally accepted.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not a defining issue; inferred from the civil-liberties stress of democratic and libertarian socialists, with authoritarian strands dissenting.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred: socialist programmes of the democratic and libertarian left generally favour decriminalisation, but the family has no common doctrine on it.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents split: authoritarian socialist states restricted speech while libertarian and many democratic socialists prioritise free expression.

strong-leader.rationale: SEP stresses that socialism means democratic control, not rule by a leader, and Luxemburg-style critics called Leninist substitutionism elitist.

state-harmful.rationale: Only anarchists see the state as unnecessary and harmful; state socialists and social democrats use it as an instrument, and Marx held it would wither away only after classes vanish.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from the democratic left's usual stance; socialist theory is silent and some traditions favour an armed working class.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred: socialists tend to favour social spending over coercive state power, though state socialist regimes built large security forces.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Socialist feminists are divided between viewing sex work as exploitation and as labour deserving rights.

decide-locally.rationale: Libertarian socialists favour federated local bodies while state socialists and social democrats favour national planning and redistribution.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from socialist views that crime reflects social conditions rather than innate character.

traditional-family.rationale: The Manifesto criticises the bourgeois family as resting on capital and private gain and proposes social education, though modern socialists do not oppose family life as such.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed in classic texts; modern socialist parties mostly support it, and the early Soviet state decriminalised homosexuality.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from socialist feminism and the modern left's emphasis on women's control over their own lives.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Manifesto treats religion as a product of material conditions, and socialist parties are generally secular, though religious socialist strands exist.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Modern socialist parties embrace anti-racism, but classic socialism centred class and the family contains class-first critics of identity-based remedies.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Socialist feminism treats women's oppression as socially and economically produced; inferred as the typical position.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Manifesto says workers have no country, yet nationalist socialist strands such as Arab socialism prize national culture.

gradual-change.rationale: Reformists seek gradual legislative change while revolutionary socialists demand rupture, so adherents are genuinely split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto's internationalism and class-not-nation framing, with labour-protectionist exceptions.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Socialist internationalism favours cooperation, but many socialists distrust the UN and other bodies as dominated by capitalist powers.

free-trade.rationale: Socialists see world trade as part of capitalist expansion and tend to demand labour and social protections, though internationalism softens opposition.

nation-first.rationale: The Manifesto holds that workers' interests are international and national divisions are fading, so putting national interest above cooperation conflicts with core internationalism.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Anti-imperialist socialists distrust interventions, but some support them; inferred and weak.

open-borders.rationale: Internationalist solidarity points toward open borders as an ideal, but socialist parties rarely endorse it as programme.

limit-growth.rationale: SEP notes socialists question the priority of growth over environment and leisure, but eco-socialists and productivist socialists disagree.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: SEP presents climate change as a critical juncture justifying expanded public action, and eco-socialism ties environmental damage to capitalist expansion.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Marx expected productive forces to enable abundance, but socialists reject techno-optimism that ignores social relations.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Socialist and eco-socialist currents are divided on nuclear power; no doctrine.

revolution-justified.rationale: Revolutionary socialists consider social revolution necessary, and the Manifesto calls for overthrow of bourgeois rule, though reformists dissent.

experts-over-public.rationale: Inferred from SEP's emphasis on democratic control and participation, against technocratic rule.

central-planning.rationale: Non-market socialism typically relies on planning and the Manifesto calls for production under a common plan, though SEP records serious doubts about information and incentives and market socialists dissent.

socialized-markets.rationale: Market socialism, with worker-managed or public firms operating in markets, is a documented strand of socialism, though Marxist non-market socialists reject markets.

land-value-tax.rationale: The Manifesto wants land rents applied to public purposes, but replacing most taxes with a land tax is a Georgist idea socialists neither adopt nor reject.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The Manifesto's measure three is abolition of the right of inheritance, so heavily taxing large inheritances falls short of the classic demand.

basic-income.rationale: SEP-type debates split socialists between a basic income as emancipation from wage dependence and as a way to prop up capitalism.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Socialists are divided between internationalist objections and protection of domestic jobs and developmental policy.

state-directs-investment.rationale: SEP lists public investment banks and democratic control of investment as socialist tools, and the Manifesto centralises credit in the state.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The Manifesto says small artisan and peasant property is being swallowed by industry and aims at common property in capital, not broad private holdings.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Marx's higher phase has producers no longer exchanging products and labour as a prime want, but SEP does not treat abolishing wage labour as a standalone goal and democratic socialists keep wages.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The Manifesto centralises credit in a state-owned national bank, the opposite of abolishing central banking.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Social democrats accept collective bargaining, but state-recognised bodies setting prices jointly with employers is corporatist, not socialist.

one-party-rule.rationale: Authoritarian socialism rejects multi-party politics, but SEP says a state without democratic control is not socialism and democratic socialists reject one-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not discussed directly; inferred from the socialist commitment to democratic control and abolition of class privilege.

democracy-best.rationale: Democratic socialism is the term most associated with socialism today and SEP holds that democracy should extend to the economy, though Leninist strands disagreed.

direct-votes.rationale: Libertarian socialists prefer direct democracy; inferred majority leaning, with representation accepted by others.

workers-councils.rationale: Workers' councils are key vehicles for libertarian socialists and council communists, but social democrats and democratic socialists rely on parliaments.

right-to-secede.rationale: Socialist traditions vary from Leninist self-determination to centralist opposition; no consensus.

natural-rulers.rationale: The Manifesto and egalitarian doctrine reject innate ruling classes, attributing class rule to property relations.

political-violence-never.rationale: Revolutionary currents accept violence and the Manifesto calls for forcible overthrow, while reformists reject it, so a flat never is a minority view.

war-builds-character.rationale: Socialists regard wars as fought for ruling classes at workers' expense; internationalism rejects glorifying war.

separate-church-state.rationale: Socialist parties are generally secular and the Manifesto treats religion as a reflection of class society, though religious socialists exist.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The Manifesto denies eternal religious truths as a basis for law, and socialism's legitimacy rests on democratic or class grounds.

private-courts-defense.rationale: SEP stresses social power and democratic control over coercive functions; private provision of defence conflicts with it.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and anti-militarism; state socialist regimes also built big militaries.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Manifesto sees nationality fading and works through class, so an ethnically defined nation is alien to core socialism.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Manifesto grounds history in class antagonism, and the class-based critique is central to socialism.

equal-outcomes.rationale: SEP says socialists seek broadly equal access to the means for flourishing, and Marx's critique of equal right aims at distribution by need, beyond mere opportunity.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred: eco-socialists and anti-colonial socialists back indigenous claims, but it is not classic doctrine.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Anti-imperialist socialists support it; classic texts do not discuss it.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred from class internationalism, though Arab socialism blended socialism with pan-Arab unity.

self-interest-moral.rationale: SEP lists community and solidarity among the core values, with competitive self-interest seen as undermining them.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Socialism is communitarian in emphasis, but democratic socialists defend individual rights and do not rank duties over them.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Eco-socialism and Morris stress nature's value, though Marxist tradition is more instrumental.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred: socialists locate poverty in social institutions rather than numbers, so they typically oppose coercive limits.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Marx held industry creates the abundance for a higher phase, so wholesale rejection is not the socialist view.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Marxist views see productive growth as the basis of socialism but not disruption for its own sake.

human-enhancement.rationale: No socialist doctrine; views range from egalitarian concern to support.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Cybernetic planning has socialist advocates, but democratic control is central, so adherents are split.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from the left's civil-liberties stance, with no doctrine.

restore-past-order.rationale: Socialism looks forward to a post-capitalist order and the Manifesto condemns reactionary attempts to restore old forms.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Socialists hold a systematic theory of society, though reformists are often pragmatic.

direct-action.rationale: Syndicalists favour direct action and the general strike, while democratic socialist and social-democratic parties work through elections.

means-match-ends.rationale: Libertarian socialists insist on prefigurative means, Leninists do not, and reformists vary.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Socialism relies on developed productive forces and abundance to reach distribution by need.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Marx's Gotha critique makes ending subordination to the division of labour and the mental-manual split a condition of the higher phase, though it is a distant goal.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Marx's formula from each according to ability, to each according to need is the best-known socialist principle, as a higher-phase aim.

production-for-use.rationale: Non-market socialism aims to remove the profit system, and SEP presents production to meet needs as a defining critique of capitalism.

profit-exploitation.rationale: SEP and the Manifesto describe surplus going to capitalists as exploitation, with bourgeois property resting on exploiting many by few.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Manifesto has the proletariat as ruling class using despotic inroads, but democratic socialists reject the dictatorship formula, so the family is split.

collective-farming.rationale: The Manifesto cultivates land under a common plan but spares small peasant property; collectivisation is a later state-socialist policy.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Leninist theory ties imperialism to capitalism, but social democrats and many socialists do not hold the inevitability claim.

taxation-theft.rationale: The Manifesto wants heavy progressive taxation, and socialists see taxes as legitimate social claims on wealth.

harm-principle.rationale: Socialists vary: liberal-leaning democratic socialists accept it while others allow wider social restraint.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Freeden-type themes stress society as more than individuals, so socialists accept collective and social rights.

conscription.rationale: Social democrats and revolutionary socialists differ, and the Manifesto lists industrial armies; no common position.

exit-over-voice.rationale: SEP's emphasis on democratic participation makes voice, not exit, the check on power.

state-as-business.rationale: Socialists see public goods as rights under democratic control, not customer services run for profit.

positive-liberty.rationale: SEP says capitalist freedom is partial because workers must sell labour to survive, so freedom requires material means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Socialists locate real power in property owners, with ruling ideas reflecting the ruling class.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not directly discussed; inferred from egalitarianism and the explanation of differences by social conditions.

organic-representation.rationale: Inferred: socialist parties are the typical vehicles, though syndicalists favour trade bodies.

total-state.rationale: SEP says a state running everything without democratic control is not socialism, though authoritarian socialist regimes approximated it.

national-rebirth.rationale: Inferred from class internationalism and rejection of nationalist myth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Socialists reject imperialist expansion and the Manifesto condemns exploitation of one nation by another.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal bonds are among the old class relations the Manifesto says capitalism and then socialism supersede.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is a class-exploitative relation socialism opposes.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The Manifesto says ruling ideas of each age are those of its ruling class and denies eternal truths.

universal-morality.rationale: The Manifesto denies eternal moral truths as products of class society, though some socialists ground ethics philosophically.

single-common-good.rationale: Socialist analysis starts from class antagonism, so politics balances or resolves class interests rather than one rational common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Labour Zionist socialists supported it, Bundists and internationalist socialists opposed it.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: No socialist doctrine; views follow positions on national self-determination.

revive-national-language.rationale: No doctrine; anti-colonial socialists often back revival while internationalists are indifferent.

workplace-democracy.rationale: SEP holds that democracy should extend beyond government into the workplace, a core socialist claim.

school-vouchers.rationale: Socialists favour universal public education and oppose market-style school choice; the Manifesto calls for free public schooling.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Inferred: socialists favour public spending and Keynesian policy as with post-war social democracy.

economic-freedom.rationale: SEP argues capitalist economic freedom is partial and that political freedom needs democratic economic control.

rule-by-example.rationale: Inferred: socialism favours democratic institutions and law.

national-self-determination.rationale: Lenin-line and anti-colonial socialists support it, while the Manifesto subordinates nation to class.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Marxist socialism is materialist and secular, but religious socialism rejects the strict claim.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from internationalism: socialists generally oppose citizen-only welfare, though labour-protectionist currents exist.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The Manifesto's equal liability to work is a duty on all, but conditioning welfare on work is a liberal or conservative policy socialists mostly oppose.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Manifesto bases politics on class antagonism, though social democrats practise partnership with employers.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Socialists want popular access to culture, not its destruction.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-imperialist socialists support non-aligned fronts, though not classic doctrine.

workers-nation.rationale: The Manifesto calls on the proletariat of all countries to unite and says workers have no country, though nationalist socialist currents exist.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Socialist feminism and the Manifesto's critique of women as instruments of production reject legally fixed roles.

ban-interest.rationale: No doctrine; Islamic socialists might favour restrictions but socialists generally prefer public control of credit.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Socialists oppose racial hierarchy and divisions that split the working class.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Manifesto says political power is the organised power of one class to oppress another, though reformists and social democrats treat the state as usable.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: SEP and eco-socialists criticise capitalism's overconsumption of fossil fuels.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred from class internationalism and pluralism.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no support in socialist analysis, which attributes immigration to labour markets.

proportional-representation.rationale: Inferred: socialist parties typically favour PR, though not doctrine.

national-mission.rationale: Socialists reject national missions of expansion and exclusion, favouring international working-class solidarity.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Socialist feminism holds women's oppression has economic and cultural sources, though classic Marxists subordinated it to class.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Socialists see elites as serving ownership interests; inferred.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics contradicts egalitarianism and environmental explanations of character.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from the left's civil-liberties stance, though state socialist regimes were themselves implicated.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Manifesto's ten measures extend the state to credit, transport, industry and education.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Race-based hierarchy contradicts class internationalism and egalitarianism.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: SEP's equality value and the Manifesto's free development of each as the condition of all imply equal worth.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Trotskyists held permanent revolution while Stalinists built socialism in one country, so the family is split.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Anti-colonial and eco-socialist currents say so; classic socialists offered no uniform view.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred from secularism and equal citizenship.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred: socialists favour freedom of conscience though some regimes suppressed religion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred as a religious-cultural measure socialists do not support.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from secularism and the Manifesto's call for social education.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Marx expected the state to wither away, and libertarian socialists dissent from Stalinist doctrine.

consent-of-governed.rationale: SEP stresses democratic control as the test of socialism.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilism is not socialist; socialists generally disfavour it.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal of minorities contradicts internationalism and equality.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Socialists accept coercive expropriation and the Manifesto calls forcible overthrow, rejecting an absolute non-aggression principle.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: SEP says competitive markets undermine solidarity, and the Manifesto sees class struggle, not interpersonal competition, as history's engine.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Socialists divided, having been both victims and users of such bans.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: SEP says workers face domination because they accept authority at work and have less political influence than owners.

separated-powers.rationale: Democratic socialists accept checks while Marxists treat them as bourgeois forms; no consensus.

vanguard-party.rationale: Leninists want a vanguard but Luxemburg and Bernstein called it elitist, and democratic strands reject it.

priority-to-poor.rationale: SEP's equality value points to prioritising basic needs, though socialism centres the working class.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Inferred: socialists favour public housing remaining public.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Unions, syndicalism and the general strike are central, so restrictions are opposed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: SEP locates poverty in exploitation and social arrangements, not numbers.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Class solidarity across ethnic lines is a core theme.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition has some libertarian-left advocates but is not doctrine.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Authoritarian socialism cited counter-revolution to restrict rights, but mainstream strands object.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Inferred from welfare and planning orientation.

party-controls-media.rationale: Authoritarian socialism restricts expression, but democratic and libertarian strands, the majority of adherents today, defend press freedom.

party-commands-army.rationale: Inferred as a Leninist practice, not general doctrine.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: A Paris Commune ideal in the Marxist tradition and modern left platforms, but not universal.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Democratic centralism is Leninist while social-democratic parties allow dissent.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Socialists divided over the EU between internationalist support and criticism as neoliberal.

clerical-rule.rationale: Socialism grounds authority in democracy or class, not religious scholars.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Class internationalism points that way, and Lenin and Luxemburg took it, but the Second International's majority backed war.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred: moralistic censorship is not socialist, though some regimes censored.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not a socialist question; practice varied.

recall-officials.rationale: Recallability was a Commune principle, though not universal in programmes.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Anti-militarist socialists favour leaving NATO-type alliances, social democrats less so.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Engels criticised the idea that tenants should become owners; inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: The idea of armed workers appears in revolutionary socialism, but mainstream does not push it.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The Manifesto seeks to erase the town-country divide, not to praise rural life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Socialist traditions have no common stance on reunifying divided nations; it turns on the local case.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Inferred: socialists value education, though populist socialism criticises intellectuals.

death-penalty.rationale: Modern socialist parties generally oppose it, though state socialist regimes used it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from socialist feminism and public education.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Socialism's materialist outlook opposes religious teaching in public education.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred from egalitarian stance and cultural autonomy debates.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The Manifesto envisions an association where each person's free development is the condition for all.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Anti-imperialist socialists support debt cancellation; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anti-colonial socialism holds that formal independence requires economic change.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: SEP says statism without democratic control is not socialism, though authoritarian regimes did so.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Socialist parties often oppose nuclear arms.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Socialism sets no rule on how a head of state is chosen; democratic accountability is the only inferred principle.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The Manifesto puts credit under state control, so independence from elected governments contradicts it.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Socialists hold bourgeois property rests on exploitation and should serve social purposes, going further than the statement.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Left-communist and Trotskyist currents say so, while Marxist-Leninists and some others call it socialist.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Manifesto treats religion as reflecting class order; socialist states limited churches, though not all agree.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Whether a head of state should be above party is a constitutional detail on which socialist parties differ.

region-keeps-system.rationale: No doctrine; arises from Chinese socialism specifically.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The Manifesto demands a heavy progressive income tax, so flat taxes are opposed.

character-from-environment.rationale: The Manifesto says consciousness changes with material conditions; utopian socialists stressed circumstances shaping people.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Socialism's democratic control requirement is incompatible.

space-expansion.rationale: Socialist theory treats productive growth as a means to abundance, not space expansion as a civilisational goal.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Inferred: socialists favour majority rule over balanced rule by few and many.

leader-cult.rationale: Mainstream rejects it, though authoritarian regimes practised it.

equal-parenting.rationale: Socialist writings do not address custody presumptions, and socialist feminists differ on the question.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Maoist idea; most socialists do not accept it.

land-redistribution.rationale: The Manifesto abolishes landed property, though it directs rents to public use rather than to farmers.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Socialism is secular and rejects penalties for belief.

women-must-cover.rationale: Socialist feminism opposes legally compelled dress.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred from class not ethnicity, though Arab socialists dissent.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The Bundist and internationalist view, but Labour Zionists dissented.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The Manifesto says ideas change with material conditions and the ruling ideas are those of the ruling class.

ban-cartels.rationale: Socialists want to replace concentrated power with social ownership, not restore competition.

no-bailouts.rationale: Socialists split between opposing bailouts of owners and favouring public takeover.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Democratic socialists prize majorities, but others defend liberal rights.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Socialist feminism and social-democratic parties often adopt gender quotas, though they are not part of classic doctrine.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inconsistent with internationalism and the Manifesto's world-market analysis.

moral-incentives.rationale: Marx's higher phase has labour as a prime want, and Guevarist socialism stressed moral incentives, though it is not a common programme.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Orthodox Marxists expect revolution from economic contradictions, and critics called Blanquism elitist.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Manifesto abolishes inheritance and ends class privilege.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred: modern left supports preferences though some class-first socialists would not.

public-money-creation.rationale: The Manifesto centralises credit in a national bank, and socialists favour public control of money.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: SEP reports socialists see capitalism as crisis-prone, though Bernstein-style reformists disagreed.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist concept only some socialists accept.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Socialists vary between rights and majoritarian views.

minority-veto.rationale: Collective democratic decisions bind the minority.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Democratic socialists favour parliament over monarchy, though councils are an alternative.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Socialist doctrine is silent on animal use, and eco-socialists and others split between welfarist and abolitionist views.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Socialists see welfare as a right of the workers, not a duty of paternal elites.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Socialism is a political movement of mass participation.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The Manifesto treats ruling ideas as those of the ruling class, though the culture-industry thesis is a later Marxist addition.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony thesis extends the Manifesto's ruling-ideas argument; not universal.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Leninist and dependency theorists hold this, but not all socialists.

party-own-road.rationale: Inferred from national-road doctrines like Eurocommunism.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Socialists back indigenous self-determination but object to ranking descendants by origin, so adherents split.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Socialist movements were central in anti-fascism; inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Socialists generally reject equating communism with fascism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Marxist materialism points to slavery as the economic cause.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred: modern socialist movements usually favour removing or recontextualising monuments to oppressors, though it is not doctrine.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Socialists favour attention to disadvantage by need, but the left is split on framing it by gender.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Socialist feminism stresses structural male advantage, while egalitarian instincts favour services for all victims, so adherents differ.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Socialists differ between universalism and national roads.

paid-care-work.rationale: Socialist feminism holds women's oppression has economic sources; wages for housework debated.

filial-duty.rationale: Socialist doctrine offers no rule on filial duty, and welfare-state socialists favour public care over family obligation.

office-by-exam.rationale: Socialists favour democratic control of office, while public-service meritocracy is a pragmatic matter on which they differ.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from public control of strategic industry.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The Manifesto criticises bourgeois marriage; inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The Paris Commune model of recallable, worker-paid delegates is celebrated in the Marxist tradition though not in all programmes.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Social democracy supports state pay-as-you-go pensions.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred: internationalist and egalitarian socialists favour minority language rights, while some socialist states imposed one language.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land is a public concern for socialists, but restricting foreign owners is a nationalist rather than socialist measure, so adherents differ.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: SEP notes socialists question growth priority, and anti-consumerism is common.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Anti-interventionist inference, though Soviet policy did so.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Contradicts democratic socialism, though Soviet practice differed.

corporate-influence.rationale: SEP says owners hold more political influence than workers.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Socialists are divided between suspicion of corporate foreign funding and defence of civil society against state control.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Socialist programmes support family benefits as social policy but have no doctrine on raising birth rates over immigration.

residents-only-property.rationale: Socialists favour local controls on housing speculation but object to excluding outsiders, so adherents split.

job-guarantee.rationale: The Manifesto's equal liability to work and left platforms favour guarantees.

democratic-peace.rationale: Marxist analysis ties wars to capitalist states.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Revolutionary socialists deny the law's authority as class rule, while democratic socialists accept legitimate democratic law.

non-intervention.rationale: Anti-imperialist socialists oppose intervention while internationalists back solidarity with revolutions, so the family is split.

industrial-unions.rationale: Syndicalism and libertarian socialism favour industrial unions.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Manifesto criticises bourgeois marriage; not universal.

informal-organisation.rationale: Mainstream socialists favour mass parties and unions.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The Manifesto says abolition targets bourgeois capital, not personal property earned by labour.

defeat-communism.rationale: Socialists oppose anti-communist crusades; the family includes communism.

religion-illusion.rationale: Marxists hold it, religious socialists do not.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Marxists see capitalism as creating productive basis, but not all socialists.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Socialist feminism holds liberation requires ending economic sources of oppression.

socialized-care.rationale: The Manifesto socialises education; social democrats offer public care.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred: linguistic purism has no place in internationalist doctrine, though some socialist nationalisms practised it.

treaties-binding.rationale: Anti-colonial socialists stress honouring treaties with indigenous nations, yet socialism has no general doctrine on them.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Utopian and libertarian strands favour it; mainstream does not.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred: socialists generally base claims on class and present need rather than historical or religious ties, with exceptions in national socialisms.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Soviet Union initially decriminalised; the left opposes.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not socialist doctrine; Islamic socialists vary.

participatory-democracy.rationale: SEP stresses democracy in workplaces, and libertarian socialists favour direct democracy.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Socialist feminism links economic and cultural sources of oppression.

assisted-dying.rationale: Socialist doctrine does not address assisted dying, and socialists divide between autonomy and concerns for vulnerable people.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Socialism is a core left position.

alienated-labor.rationale: SEP presents alienation, work that blocks self-realisation, as a defining socialist critique, and the Gotha text imagines labour becoming life's prime want only after the division of labour is overcome.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred: socialism's universalist, class-based outlook rejects blaming a religion's followers.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Socialists ground authority in the people and the working class, and the Manifesto treats religion as ideology of the ruling order.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Adherents are split between secular-state and religious-freedom positions.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from its concern for workers' rights against employers; not discussed in the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: Socialism seeks social ownership of the main means of production, not merely a regulated market economy.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Inferred: Marx opposed standing armies and favoured arming the people, but socialists generally do not call for abolishing armed forces outright.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from its core egalitarian aim of common ownership and distribution by need.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Foreign alignment is outside the family's defining doctrine and adherents are split.

missingStatements.text: Capitalism by its nature produces recurring economic crises.
missingStatements.rationale: SEP lists crisis-proneness, underprovision of public goods and externalities among socialists' core criticisms of capitalism.

missingStatements.text: Work under capitalism alienates people from their own creative activity.
missingStatements.rationale: SEP presents alienation, work that blocks self-realisation, as a defining socialist critique, and Marx's Gotha text imagines labour becoming a prime want of life.

notes: Socialism is a broad family; the profile follows the documented majority and scores 0 where democratic, libertarian, Leninist and social-democratic strands genuinely split.
